title: Hourly to Annual Pay: Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top – Including Minimum Wage UK Comparisons
description: Convert hourly rate to annual salary with 38-hour week, casual loading, and super. Compare with minimum wage UK rules for context.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with super paid on top.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my hourly to annual conversion?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% on top of the base hourly rate, compensating for not receiving paid leave. When converting to annual pay, you multiply the loaded rate by hours per week and 52. For example, the national minimum wage of $26.44/hour becomes $33.05/hour with casual loading, giving an annual gross of $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80 before super and tax.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the annual pay figure?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. So if your annual gross is $65,306.80, your employer would contribute an extra $7,836.82 to your super fund, not included in your take-home pay.

faqs.q: How does the minimum wage uk compare to Australia's national minimum wage?
faqs.a: The UK has its own minimum wage calculation rules, as detailed in. Unlike Australia's single national minimum wage of $26.44/hour for adults, the UK has age-based rates and different treatment of overtime premiums. In Australia, casual loading of 25% is added for employees without paid leave, while the UK does not have a universal casual loading. Always check the relevant Fair Work award for your industry.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Hourly to Annual Pay in Australia

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, converting between the two helps you compare jobs and plan your finances. The standard formula in Australia is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. For full-time employees, the typical week is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission. If you work part-time or casual, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

### The Fortnightly View

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. For example, if your weekly gross is $1,004.90 (the national minimum wage for 38 hours), your fortnightly gross is $2,009.80 before tax and super.

## National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the national minimum wage is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for 38 ordinary hours, according to the Fair Work Commission. This is the base rate for adult employees not covered by an award or agreement. However, most employees are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or role. Always check the relevant award using [pay guides](/blog) or the [reference tables](/data) on this site.

### Casual Loading

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base rate. This compensates for not receiving paid sick leave or annual leave. When converting your hourly rate to annual pay, you should apply the loading first. For example:

- Base rate: $26.44/hour
- Casual rate: $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05/hour
- Annual gross (38 hours/week): $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80

Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into the [timesheet](/); the checkbox will add the 25% for you.

## Superannuation Paid on Top

Superannuation is not part of your salary; it is paid on top by your employer. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). So if your annual gross is $65,306.80, your employer contributes an additional $7,836.82 to your super fund. This amount is not included in your take-home pay but grows for your retirement.

For more details on how super interacts with your pay, see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax and Medicare Levy

Your take-home pay is your gross pay minus tax and the Medicare levy. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,370 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. This estimate does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

## Comparing with Minimum Wage UK

While this guide focuses on Australia, it is useful to understand how the minimum wage uk differs. The UK has separate minimum wage rates for different age groups and apprentices, and its calculation rules exclude overtime premiums and shift allowances from the minimum wage pay. In contrast, Australia’s national minimum wage is a single adult rate, with junior rates as a percentage of that. The UK also does not have a universal casual loading like Australia’s 25%.

If you are comparing job offers between the two countries, remember that Australian superannuation is paid on top of your salary, while UK pension contributions may be deducted from your pay. Always use the official sources for each country.

## Using the Timesheet

Our [timesheet](/) helps you convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Simply enter your base hourly rate (before casual loading) and check the casual loading box if applicable. The calculator uses the 38-hour week assumption but you can adjust the hours. It also estimates tax and super based on the latest ATO and Fair Work data.

For more detailed breakdowns, explore [average pay](/topics/average-pay) or [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) topics.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
